summary: In major international human spaceflight developments, China unveiled its new space station crew, which features a Pakistani astronaut scheduled to board the orbital platform, while a pair of spacecraft successfully entered orbit around Mercury. In civil and military space operations, Officer Training School graduated the U.S. Space Force's first all-Guardian squadron, NASA awarded a contract for NOAA’s Near Earth Orbit Network Program, and the U.S. Air Force clarified that a $16 billion propulsion mega-contract announcement was posted in error. Civil space planning also expanded as NASA announced it is seeking industry partners to design the first nuclear reactor for the Moon. Commercial launch and orbital technology maintained rapid momentum, with SpaceX establishing a pad turnaround record by launching two rockets 32 hours apart, three recent launches advancing a military space data network backbone, and satellite operators Umbra and ICEYE introducing higher-resolution radar imaging capabilities. In space science, researchers successfully cultivated potatoes in simulated lunar dust, a rocket flight test demonstrated the durability of a protective coating for space medicine, and data from the James Webb Space Telescope yielded new findings on early black hole growth and supernova dust evolution. Readers should watch for today's scheduled launch of an Ariane 6 rocket carrying 36 Amazon LEO satellites into orbit.
